label: input m at position 2, gated by the first two tokens (first token r/x, or second token m/d/0)
explanation: Very sparse reset-gate unit that fires almost only (99% of activation mass) when the third original token (t=2) is m. Only about 11% of m-at-t=2 steps fire, and whether it fires depends on the two preceding tokens in a roughly additive way: first token r or x (lift 6x and 4x) and second token m, d or 0 (lift 8x, 8x, 5x) raise the activation, and u/w/o raise it a little. The strongest activations are r m m, x m m and r d m. Tiny residual: a few firings at t=3 (e.g. r z d m, or <DEL> after r z d), and on p/k at t=2. It never fires in the copy phase or on m at any other position. Because the dependence on the prefix is graded, a crisp predicate trades precision against recall: using only (t=2 and in=m) gets recall 0.96 and precision 0.11, while the chosen OR of first-token and second-token sets gets dev F1 0.68 and mass recall 0.91.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 34 cues. Raise it: t=2 & prev_tok=m (+3.53), t=2 & in_tok=m (+3.35), t=2 & prev_tok=u (+3.03), orig0=r (+3.03), prev_tok=d (+2.35), t=2 & prev_tok=0 (+2.31). Lower it: prev2_tok=v (-1.64), prev2_tok=a (-1.52), in_first=0 (-1.42), orig4=v (-1.07).
